$comment: Deterministic transforms for vendored files (tools/sync). Rules run in this order; each is scoped by "files" or "glob":
"files": the tier 2 files it must change; a listed file it no longer changes fails the sync, and so does a vendored file it matches without listing it.
"glob": every vendored file (tier 1 or 2) the pattern matches, wherever it matches; it must change at least one file. Only for repo-wide renames.
A rule either rewrites ("find": a JavaScript regex, global, plus optional "flags" from imsu; "replace": $1..$9 for groups, $$ for $)
or drops a member ("drop": a regex matching its declaration in code, exactly once per listed file; its lines are left blank, so line numbers match upstream's).
Fix the rule, never the vendored file. The library's rules (from #1) come first; the namespace rename runs last, so every other rule is written against upstream's text.

rules.why: The WinUIEx-derived code (Hosting/) is tier 3 and never vendored, so its notice doesn't apply here, and it names a person (CLAUDE.md: no personal data). Yoga's notice, which does apply, is kept.

Generator name table: Avalonia's routed CLR events (Button.Click) are EventHandler<RoutedEventArgs>.
Generator name table: argument types not worth surfacing.

Generator logic hunk 1: the {Prop}Property member is any static AvaloniaProperty (StyledProperty, DirectProperty, AttachedProperty), not a WinUI DependencyProperty. Helper in the generator project's WrapperGenerator.Avalonia.cs.

rules.find:
for \(INamedTypeSymbol\? t = control; t is not null; t = t\.BaseType\)?
\s*foreach \(var a in t\.GetAttributes\(\)\)?
\s*if \(a\.AttributeClass\?\.ToDisplayString\(SymbolDisplayFormat\.FullyQualifiedFormat\)?
\s*== "global::Microsoft\.UI\.Xaml\.Markup\.ContentPropertyAttribute"\)(?
\s*)\{?
\s*var name = a\.NamedArguments\.FirstOrDefault\(na => na\.Key == "Name"\)\.Value\.Value as string?
\s*\?\? \(a\.ConstructorArguments\.Length > 0 \? a\.ConstructorArguments\[0\]\.Value as string : null\);?
\s*if \(name is null\) continue;
rules.why: Generator logic hunk 2: WinUI names the content property in a class-level [ContentProperty(Name=...)]; Avalonia marks the property itself with [Content]. Helper in WrapperGenerator.Avalonia.cs.
Generator logic hunk 3a: grouped controlled bindings keep their per-control state in an Avalonia attached property (WinUI: DependencyProperty.RegisterAttached).
Generator logic hunk 3b: the event owner gate is an Avalonia attached property too.
Our rule: [Obsolete] control properties aren't surfaced (Avalonia 12's TextBox keeps Watermark, WatermarkForeground and UseFloatingWatermark as obsolete aliases).

Our rule: Avalonia's ItemCollection implements IList and IReadOnlyList<object?>, not IList<object>, so items controls (ListBox, ComboBox, TabControl, Carousel, TreeView) qualify for the items-host strategy through IList too.
Our rule: the items-host strategy takes an IList<object>; ItemsList.Of passes one through and adapts a non-generic IList (the library's Seam/V1Protocol/ItemsList.cs).

rules.replace: $1        var missingCounterpart = descriptorOnly ? MissingCounterparts(element, control, props, contentProp is null ? null : contentElementName, panelChildren, items, exclude) : null;$1$2
rules.why: Our rule: in descriptor-only mode a record member with no same-name control property the generator can map was silently dropped; now it's reported (ISOTOPEGEN001, WrapperGenerator.Avalonia.cs).
Our rule: the descriptor-only output reports the missing-counterpart diagnostic with its source.

rules.replace: { } // Avalonia: no XAML metadata provider to register
rules.why: Our rule: full-wrapper mode registered the control assembly's WinUI XAML metadata provider (ReactorApp.TryRegisterControlAssembly); Avalonia has none, so nothing is emitted.
WinUI and Composition namespace imports: the names they brought in come from global aliases onto Avalonia types (Seam/GlobalUsings.cs) or from the rules below.
WinUI types named through upstream's `using WinUI = Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls;` alias: use the bare name, which the global aliases map to Avalonia.
WinUI's EffectiveViewportChanged handler shape, as Avalonia's Layoutable.EffectiveViewportChanged declares it.
WinUI's Loaded handler shape, as Avalonia's Control.Loaded declares it.
Fully qualified WinUI identity types: drop the namespace so the global aliases map them to Avalonia's Control.
WinUI's DispatcherQueue, fully qualified: the bare name resolves to the internal Avalonia-dispatcher wrapper in Seam/Threading.cs.
Windows' app memory-pressure API, fully qualified: the bare names resolve to internal placeholders in Seam/Tier3Placeholders.cs (no memory-pressure signal on Avalonia yet).
